task.description: Run the full INV-1..INV-8 gate against git diff main...HEAD, focused on lib/letflow/definitions/snapshot_store.ex (new module, Letflow.Definitions.SnapshotStore). Pay particular attention to: (a) INV-1 prefix scoping, (b) INV-7 FOR SHARE lock via Ecto.Query.lock/2 not raw SQL, (c) independently re-verify ELIXIR-DEV's self-reported Ecto.UUID.cast/1 guard fix against real malformed/struct-shaped input, (d) answer OQ-1 (cross-tenant definition_id vs nonexistent) from a security perspective.
acceptance_criteria: scope test explicitly run and recorded against the actual diff
every applicable INV-1..INV-8 invariant checked with its How-to-verify procedure and recorded PASS/FAIL
the UUID-cast INV-8 fix independently re-verified against real malformed/struct-shaped input, not trusted from ELIXIR-DEV's self-report
OQ-1's cross-tenant definition_id question explicitly answered from a security perspective

result.summary:
Scope test: run explicitly against git diff main...HEAD (git diff --stat confirms the only application-code file touched is lib/letflow/definitions/snapshot_store.ex, new). IN SCOPE (tenant-data path) -- create/3 reads process_definitions and writes instance_definition_snapshots, get_by_instance_id/2 reads instance_definition_snapshots; both tables are tenant-scoped via Postgres schema (:prefix), neither operation touches a tenant_id column this module writes.

Read docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md in full (not from memory) -- confirmed INV-1's 2026-08-17 addendum: S1 done, S2 migrations exist, INV-1 is live now, not a default skip.

INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. (a) Every Repo call in the module passes prefix: explicitly -- confirmed by direct grep/read of all 4 Repo entry points: locked_source_definition/2's Repo.one(prefix: prefix) (line 180), Repo.insert(..., prefix: prefix) (line 204), Repo.get(..., prefix: prefix) twice (lines 141, 207). fetch_prefix/1 (lines 154-159) requires opts[:prefix] to be a non-empty binary or returns {:error, :missing_prefix} before any I/O -- there is no default/fallback branch that could silently use a blank prefix; empirically confirmed (see INV-8 evidence below) that omitting :prefix, or passing nil/empty-string/integer, all short-circuit to {:error, :missing_prefix} without reaching any Repo call. (b) Both migrations creating the tables this module touches (priv/repo/migrations/20260816193001_create_process_definitions.exs, 20260816193002_create_instance_definition_snapshots.exs) are wrapped in `if prefix() do ... end` -- read both migrations directly, confirmed neither table is reachable in the public/default schema. (c) tenant_id column: instance_definition_snapshots has no tenant_id column at all (confirmed by reading InstanceDefinitionSnapshot's schema block, lib/letflow/definitions/instance_definition_snapshot.ex lines 93-104 -- only instance_id/definition_id/definition_name/definition_ver/graph/snapshotted_at). process_definitions does carry tenant_id (confirmed in the migration), but this module never writes to process_definitions -- locked_source_definition/2 is a read-only Repo.one under FOR SHARE, no insert/update against that table anywhere in the diff. No caller-supplied tenant_id field exists anywhere in this module's public API. INV-1 satisfied on all three sub-checks.

INV-2/INV-3/INV-5 -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No API response-shaping code (S4 not started), no scripting sandbox (S5 not started), no lookup-by-ID HTTP endpoint (get_by_instance_id/2 is an internal context function, not a route).

INV-4 (secrets) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. grep -n 'System.get_env|password|secret|token' against snapshot_store.ex: zero hits. This diff resolves no secret material.

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove scoping) -- APPLIES, satisfied by this handoff's explicit per-invariant statement (this document).

INV-7 (no raw SQL) -- APPLIES, PASS. grep -rn 'Repo.query' lib/ priv/repo/migrations/ finds hits only in lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex, lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex, lib/letflow/sandbox_pool/fixture_loader.ex -- none of which are part of this diff (confirmed via git diff main...HEAD --stat, only snapshot_store.ex/design doc/handoffs changed); pre-existing and out of this review's scope. snapshot_store.ex itself has zero Repo.query calls. The FOR SHARE lock (locked_source_definition/2, lines 176-181) uses `ProcessDefinition |> where(...) |> lock("FOR SHARE") |> Repo.one(prefix: prefix)` -- Ecto.Query composition, not a hand-built SQL string. Independently verified, not just read: ran Ecto.Adapters.SQL.to_sql(:all, Repo, query) against the exact same query construction (import Ecto.Query; ProcessDefinition |> where([d], d.id == ^definition_id) |> lock("FOR SHARE")) via `mix run` against this host's real Postgres config. Result: `SELECT ... FROM "process_definitions" AS p0 WHERE (p0."id" = $1) FOR SHARE`, params: [<<...16 raw uuid bytes...>>] -- definition_id is bound as a query parameter ($1), never string-interpolated; the only literal text in the emitted SQL is the fixed "FOR SHARE" hint, which is a hardcoded developer-supplied string in the source (never built from tenant/caller input), exactly the lock/2 usage pattern INV-7's Reference section describes as safe.

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes) -- APPLIES, PASS, independently re-verified with real function calls against real compiled code (not trusted from ELIXIR-DEV's self-report). Ran `mix compile --force` (clean, 48 files, no warnings) then `mix run` against a script (MIX_ENV=dev, real Postgres on localhost:5462 via docker) that called SnapshotStore.create/3 and SnapshotStore.get_by_instance_id/2 with 10 malformed/struct-shaped values each (nil, empty string, non-UUID string, integer, atom, list, plain map, a real struct (DateTime.utc_now()), a real Ecto struct (%ProcessDefinition{}), and a tuple) against instance_id, and separately against definition_id for create/3, plus 4 malformed/missing :prefix cases. All 34 calls returned typed {:error, :invalid_instance_id} / {:error, :invalid_definition_id} / {:error, :missing_prefix} tuples -- zero raises, zero CastError, across both functions and every value shape tried, including the struct-shaped inputs the design doc's original assumption (changeset-mediated cast) would not have caught for get_by_instance_id/2 (which never builds a changeset at all) or for create/3's L1 locked read (which runs before any changeset exists). This empirically confirms the fix is complete for both call sites, not merely plausible from reading the source. Checked for other fields with the same gap: the only two caller-supplied identifiers reaching a Repo call anywhere in this module are instance_id and definition_id, both guarded by cast_uuid/2 before any query is composed; the prefix value is validated as a non-empty binary by fetch_prefix/1 (also pre-I/O); all other fields written (definition_name, definition_ver, graph) are copied from an already-loaded %ProcessDefinition{} struct (trusted, DB-sourced, not caller input) and go through InstanceDefinitionSnapshot.create_changeset/2's Ecto.Changeset.cast/3, which is designed to handle arbitrary attrs shapes without raising (returns changeset errors, never CastError) -- no gap there. Heuristic grep `^\s*{:ok, .*} = ` against snapshot_store.ex: zero hits.

OQ-1 (cross-tenant definition_id indistinguishable from nonexistent) -- answered from a security perspective as requested: this is safe/expected behavior, not a real tenant-isolation gap. locked_source_definition/2's WHERE d.id == ^definition_id runs with prefix: prefix bound to opts[:prefix]'s own physical Postgres schema (confirmed by the to_sql probe above -- the query has no cross-schema UNION, no dynamic schema search_path widening, nothing that could see a row in a different tenant's physical schema). A definition_id belonging to another tenant's process_definitions row is therefore not merely permission-denied but physically invisible to this query -- Postgres schema-per-tenant isolation (0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md Dimension B) makes the row not exist from this connection's vantage point, the same guarantee already relied on for every other tenant-scoped table in this codebase (instance_sequence/event_idempotency per req025-event-append.md's INV-AP-9, cited by this design's own §3). The resulting behavior -- :definition_not_found, identical to a genuinely nonexistent definition_id -- is in fact the textbook correct answer to INV-5's not-found/forbidden-indistinguishability concern (not yet formally applicable since no HTTP endpoint exists, but the same principle: no differential signal leaks whether a cross-tenant row exists). There is no code path in this module that could special-case a cross-tenant hit into a different, more informative response even if someone wanted to -- the physical schema boundary forecloses it before the query runs, not after a check. Confirms the design doc's own OQ-1 answer rather than accepting it uncritically: re-derived independently from the actual SQL/params the query composition produces, not from the design doc's prose alone.

Overall: all applicable invariants (INV-1, INV-4 N/A, INV-6, INV-7, INV-8; INV-2/INV-3/INV-5 N/A) PASS. No FAIL found on any applicable invariant.
